whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Wrongful Death Claim

items.title: Standing Is Limited by Law
items.desc: California only allows certain people, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, to file a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs eligible under specific circumstances. An attorney can help determine who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: The Clock Starts Running Fast
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity, like a public road authority, may be involved. Waiting to get guidance can cost your family the chance to recover anything at all.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: California law allows families to seek recovery for funeral and burial costs, lost financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. A civil wrongful death case is separate from any criminal charges that may also result from the same incident.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Seaside?
items.answer: Generally, California law allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If the claim involves a government entity, such as a city road or public agency, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early formal claim. Because these timelines are strict, it helps to speak with an attorney as soon as you're able.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: California law gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children to bring the claim. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify depending on the specific family situation. An independent attorney can review the details and explain who has standing in your case.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on a busy Seaside road like Fremont Boulevard?
items.answer: Public crash records show corridors like Fremont Boulevard and Del Monte Boulevard see notable traffic volume, particularly on Friday evenings, but that alone doesn't determine legal responsibility. What matters is the specific facts of how the incident happened, which is something an attorney would investigate. LawProactive can connect you with someone who can look into the details on your family's behalf.

items.question: What compensation can a wrongful death claim recover?
items.answer: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and compensation for the loss of their companionship and guidance. There's no way to know in advance what a specific case may be worth, but an attorney can walk you through what applies to your situation. This is a civil matter, separate from any criminal proceedings connected to the same event.
